50544302.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human WDR5 by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Instruments, Worcestershire, UK) at 25 °C. The WDR5 protein (100 μM) was loaded into the sample cell, and the compound (2 mM) was loaded into the syringe. The titration consisted of 20 injections of 2 μL each, with a 120 s spacing between injections. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (OriginLab, Northampton, MA, USA) to fit a single-site binding model. The binding affinity (Kd) was calculated from the binding isotherm. The buffer used was 20 mM HEPES (pH 7.4), 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, and 0.02% NaN3. The experiments were performed in triplicate, and the results were averaged. A blank experiment with buffer in the syringe was performed to correct for heat of dilution.
original_paragraph.Figure 4 caption: Fig. 4. Binding affinity of compounds 30, 41 and 42 evaluated with ITC. Upper panels show heat of binding plotted versus time. Lower panels show fit to a single-site binding model to the binding isotherms. Kd (S.D.) derived from the fit is indicated.

assay_conditions.buffer_composition: 20 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, 0.02% NaN3
assay_conditions.control_method: A blank experiment with buffer in the syringe was performed to correct for heat of dilution
